Hi Emily,

Thanks again for the demo last week — great to see OakBridge's chat workflow and the bursty embedding backfill you mentioned. Per our conversation, I wanted to put a concise recommendation on pilot scope, packaging, and the runtime knobs that will most impact your unit economics so we can get to a mutual action plan.

Top-line suggestion: run a 6-week pilot that exercises both the low-latency interactive chat path and a daytime batch embeddings job. That lets us validate: (a) quantization impact on downstream quality for your summarization use-case, (b) batching + cache hit rates on typical traffic, and (c) operational fallbacks for peak traffic.

Pilot sketch (high level):
- Duration: 6 weeks (4w evaluation + 2w buffer)
- Scope: chat (p99 latency target 150ms for requests <=512 tokens), embeddings (backfill batch jobs up to 1M rows over pilot)
- Capacity: reserve a small Dedicated pool + hosted burst for daytime spikes (we recommend a 2-GPU dedicated pod for baseline throughput)
- Credits: 50k free credits for the pilot (applies to token usage & embeddings), conversion credit if you sign within 30 days

Runtime & quantization guidance (quick):
- For interactive chat: prefer q4_k_m or int8 where supported to keep latency low and quality high. Avoid aggressive 3-bit quant profiles initially — they can introduce hallucination for long summarization chains.
- For embeddings/batch: int4 with higher batch sizes is usually fine and yields substantial cost savings. Enable prefix/KV cache for repeated contexts during chat sessions: we often see 20–40% token cost reduction.

I've attached a short term sheet and a technical note with suggested config options. If this framing looks reasonable, I'd like to confirm a pilot start date next week and loop in procurement for the paperwork.

Next steps:
1) Tell me if the pilot scope is aligned with OakBridge priorities.
2) If yes, pick a target start (we can aim for 2027-06-21).
3) I'll loop in Karthik for the fine-grained quant/batching config and Marissa for commercial/terms.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Jordan

Jordan / Marissa / Emily — quick technical note and suggested artifacts.

1) Quantization and quality guidance:
- Interactive chat (low latency): start with q4_k_m when model filter supports it (we see best quality/latency tradeoff for summarization prompts). Fallback to int8 if you observe any regression at tail sequences. Avoid int3/3-bit on summarization until we run per-prompt evals.
- Embeddings (throughput-first): int4 is recommended; batch size >=64 on CPU fallback and >=128 on GPU gives good throughput.

2) Golden prompts / evaluation artifacts (we'll include the PDF):
- 12 canonical prompts (mix of short Q/A, 512-token summarization, multi-turn user context) for quality checks.
- Simple metric sheet: embedding cosine similarity on labeled pairs; ROUGE/L score for summarization outputs.

3) Runtime knobs and kernel selection:
- Kernel selection: we recommend using our optimized fused-attention kernel for sequences <=1024 to keep p99 latency low.
- KV caching: enable prefix cache for active chat session IDs; expect 20–35% token cost reduction on repeat prompts.
- Batching: continuous batching for embeddings jobs with max latency budget of 2s; for chat keep max batch window = 20ms to preserve latency SLO.

4) Pilot sizing suggestion:
- Daily baseline: 100k tokens/day for chat (mixed short/medium), embeddings backfill: up to 1M rows across pilot spread over weekdays.
- Reserved compute: 2-GPU dedicated for chat plus a burst pool on hosted for <5% peak overflow.

I'll attach the detailed recommendations PDF. Happy to jump on a 30-min call with OakBridge eng to walk through kernels and tradeoffs.

—Karthik
